input: Research co-housing intentional living communities nearby

keyUnknowns.whyItMatters: Co-housing and intentional communities cover a wide spectrum — from urban co-ops to rural ecovillages to senior co-housing — and knowing which types to include or exclude shapes the entire research focus.
"Nearby" is undefined — the user's location and how far a radius they consider acceptable determines which communities are even relevant.
Whether this is for a single person, a couple, a family with kids, or seniors changes which communities are a fit, since many have specific demographic compositions or requirements.
Co-housing ranges from affordable rentals to expensive ownership buy-ins; the user's budget ceiling determines which options are worth investigating.
Is the user casually curious, actively looking to move, or wanting to visit and connect? The depth of research and the output format depend on how close to a decision they are.
Different communities have strong identities — ecological focus, spiritual practice, political values, social structure — and knowing what resonates (or is a dealbreaker) focuses the shortlist.
The user may want a simple list, a comparison table, direct contact details, or help scheduling tours — the next concrete action depends on what format is most useful to them.

gold.taskDescription: Find and evaluate co-housing or intentional living communities in the user's local area as a potential place to live or connect with.

questions.title: Which types of community are you open to exploring?
questions.description: Clarify whether the user wants to focus on co-housing specifically, or also include ecovillages, housing co-ops, intentional communities, or other models.

questions.title: What city or region should "nearby" be centred on?
questions.description: Get the user's location and the maximum distance or commute they consider acceptable.

questions.title: Who would be moving or joining — just you, a partner, kids?
questions.description: Determine the household composition so communities with age or family-structure requirements can be filtered appropriately.

questions.title: What is your rough budget for buy-in, rent, or monthly fees?
questions.description: Establish a financial ceiling to exclude communities that are out of reach and prioritise affordable or ownership options accordingly.

questions.title: Are you actively ready to move, or still in early exploration mode?
questions.description: Understand how close to a decision the user is, which determines how deep and actionable the research needs to be.

questions.title: What values or lifestyle priorities matter most to you in a community?
questions.description: Identify non-negotiables and dealbreakers such as ecological focus, shared meals, spiritual practice, political alignment, or social structure.

questions.title: What output would be most useful — a list, a comparison table, or contact details?
questions.description: Determine the format and immediate next action the user wants from this research effort.
